hello.note: The final は is read wa, not ha.

goodbye.note: Sounds final; day to day people say では、また (de wa, mata) or 失礼します (shitsurei shimasu).

please.note: For asking. When offering or inviting ("please, go ahead"): どうぞ (dōzo).

thank_you.text: ありがとうございます

youre_welcome.note: Often people just say いいえ (iie), "not at all".

yes.note: Also signals "I'm listening", not always agreement.

no.note: Can sound blunt; people soften it: いえ、大丈夫です (ie, daijōbu desu), "no, I'm fine".

sorry.note: Less formal than すみません (sumimasen), which is safer with strangers and at work. Among friends: ごめん (gomen).

excuse_me.note: Often preceded by あの (ano): あの、すみません. The same word also means "sorry".

good_morning.note: Among friends and family: おはよう (ohayō).

how_are_you.note: Asked after some time apart, not as an everyday greeting.

im_fine.text: 元気です、ありがとうございます
im_fine.note: A warmer, very Japanese reply: おかげさまで元気です (okagesama de genki desu).

whats_your_name.note: More polite: お名前を伺ってもいいですか (onamae o ukagatte mo ii desu ka).

my_name_is.note: Natives often drop 私は and just say …です. More formal: …と申します (… to mōshimasu).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Usually followed by よろしくお願いします (yoroshiku onegai shimasu).

where_from.text: どちらからいらっしゃいましたか？
where_from.note: Simpler: どこから来ましたか (doko kara kimashita ka).

im_from.note: Also common: …出身です (… shusshin desu).

speak_english.note: Softer: 英語は大丈夫ですか (eigo wa daijōbu desu ka).

speak_slowly.text: もう少しゆっくり話してください

where.note: On its own, どこ？ (doko?) is casual.

what.note: On its own, 何？ (nani?) is casual. 何 is read nan before です.

why.note: Also なぜ (naze), more formal, or なんで (nande), casual.

who.note: Politer: どなたですか (donata desu ka).

where_bathroom.note: Politer: お手洗いはどこですか (otearai wa doko desu ka).

can_you_help.text: 手伝っていただけますか？
can_you_help.note: For help with a task. If you are in trouble: 助けてもらえますか (tasukete moraemasu ka).

what_means.text: これはどういう意味ですか？
what_means.roman: Kore wa dō iu imi desu ka?

four.note: Also read shi, but yon is preferred: shi sounds like 死, "death".

seven.note: Also read shichi; nana is clearer and more common on its own.

nine.note: Also read ku, but kyū is more common on its own.

water.note: In restaurants people say お水 (omizu).

tea.note: Means green tea by default; black tea is 紅茶 (kōcha).

bread.note: Borrowed from Portuguese pão centuries ago.

menu_please.text: メニューをお願いします

bill_please.text: お会計をお願いします
bill_please.note: Also お勘定 (okanjō). In many places you pay at the register by the door.

delicious.note: Politer, e.g. to a host: おいしいです (oishii desu).

no_meat.note: Vegetarian: ベジタリアンです (bejitarian desu).

enjoy_meal.note: Said by those about to eat. A host inviting guests to eat says どうぞ召し上がってください (dōzo meshiagatte kudasai).

straight_ahead.note: Go straight on: まっすぐ行ってください (massugu itte kudasai).

stop_here.text: ここで止めてください
stop_here.note: Also very common: ここでお願いします (koko de onegai shimasu).

want_to_go.note: To a taxi driver: …までお願いします (… made onegai shimasu).

one_ticket.text: 切符を一枚お願いします
one_ticket.note: 一枚 (ichimai) is "one" for flat things such as tickets.

too_expensive.note: Haggling is unusual in most Japanese shops.

cheaper.text: もう少し安いのはありますか？
cheaper.roman: Mō sukoshi yasui no wa arimasu ka?

id_like_this.note: Also これにします (kore ni shimasu), "I'll take this one".

just_looking.note: In speech often shortened to 見てるだけです (miteru dake desu).

pay_card.note: Also common: カード使えますか (kādo tsukaemasu ka).

closed.note: Literally "preparing", the flip side of 営業中. Closed all day: 本日休業 (honjitsu kyūgyō).

tomorrow.note: Also read asu (a little formal) or myōnichi (very formal, e.g. business).

good_night.note: Before sleep; casual おやすみ (oyasumi). Leaving somewhere at night: 失礼します (shitsurei shimasu).

see_you_later.note: For the next day: また明日 (mata ashita).

wait_moment.text: ちょっと待ってください
wait_moment.note: Staff say the formal 少々お待ちください (shōshō omachi kudasai).

call_police.text: 警察を呼んでください！
call_police.note: The police number in Japan is 110, said hyakutōban.

need_doctor.text: 医者に診てもらいたいです
need_doctor.note: Literally "I'd like a doctor to see me". Urgent: 医者を呼んでください (isha o yonde kudasai).

dont_feel_well.note: Feeling sick or nauseous: 気分が悪いです (kibun ga warui desu).

pharmacy.note: Drugstores, ドラッグストア (doraggusutoa), also sell basic medicine.

hospital.note: Careful: 美容院 (biyōin) is a hair salon.

allergic.note: の is often dropped: 卵アレルギーがあります (tamago arerugī ga arimasu), egg allergy.

be_careful.note: As a sudden warning shout: 危ない！ (abunai!), "watch out!"

no_problem.note: More formal: 問題ありません (mondai arimasen).

maybe.note: Also かもしれません (kamo shiremasen) at the end of a sentence: "it might be".

dont_know.text: ちょっとわかりません
dont_know.note: ちょっと softens it. 知りません (shirimasen) also means "I don't know" but can sound curt.

i_like_it.note: About something just seen or received: 気に入りました (ki ni irimashita).

dont_like_it.text: あまり好きではありません
dont_like_it.note: あまり ("not very") softens it. Conversational: 好きじゃないです (suki ja nai desu).

im_tired.note: Past form, as in "I've got tired". Casual: 疲れた (tsukareta).

im_happy.note: Happy about something that just happened. Happy in life: 幸せです (shiawase desu).

welcome.note: Shops and restaurants greet customers with いらっしゃいませ (irasshaimase).

congratulations.text: おめでとうございます！
